question: Should OpenClaw core own this private restored-admission and recovery-journal seam, with external hosts retaining ingress fencing, wake, placement, durable acceptance, and compute retirement?
rationale: The patch is a technically bounded implementation, but the durable API and operational ownership boundary determine whether it should become supported core behavior; that choice cannot be inferred safely from tests or a single host proof.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow core seam
options.body: Accept the proposed split, then review and land the stacked recovery slices as the initial private OpenClaw contract.

options.title: Keep recovery orchestration host-owned
options.body: Decline the core seam and ask for any reusable missing primitive to be proposed separately with a smaller contract.

options.title: Pause for RFC revision
options.body: Keep the PR open but defer merge until the RFC specifies lifecycle ownership, support expectations, and upgrade semantics.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow core seam
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed split, then review and land the stacked recovery slices as the initial private OpenClaw contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent restart-recovery admission work is the closest evidence-backed ownership signal for the Gateway admission boundary.
